o: Heavenly Father, I thank You for this new day You give me. I open my eyes and acknowledge that every morning is a sign of Your faithfulness. Your mercies never come to an end, and Your love has sustained me since before I awoke. Today I come before You with a simple heart, wanting to listen to You before I go out to do my tasks.

Lord, sometimes I feel small and think that what I do does not matter. Teach me to see with Your eyes. You take what is small and make it grow; You use what is humble to carry Your light to others. Give me courage today to sow a good word, a gesture of kindness, a silent prayer for someone who needs it, even if no one sees it. Keep my tongue from complaint and fill my hands with service.

Give me wisdom for the decisions of this day, patience with the people I will meet and faith to believe that You are at work even when I see no results. Take care of my family, my friends and those who are suffering right now. May my whole day be pleasing to You, and at its close may I be able to say that I walked at Your side. I place my plans, my fears and my hopes in Your hands. In Jesus' name, amen.
h: On this day, November 7, 1918, a boy named William Franklin Graham, whom the world would know as Billy Graham, was born in Charlotte, North Carolina. No one could then imagine that this child, raised in the simple setting of a dairy farm, would preach the Gospel to crowds in many countries.

Already as a young man, Billy embraced faith in Jesus Christ and felt the call to proclaim his name. He studied at the Florida Bible Institute, was ordained in 1940 by the Southern Baptist Convention and graduated from Wheaton College in Illinois in 1943. Over the years, his crusades carried the message of the cross to cities around the world, and his invitation was always the same: return to God and trust in Christ as Savior.

Billy Graham died in February 2018, at the age of 99. Millions of people remember him not so much for his fame as for his insistence that the Bible is the center of everything and that Jesus is the only way to the Father. His life began in a humble place and ended leaving a mark on entire generations.

His story reminds us of what Jesus taught with a tiny seed. God does not need to begin with something big to do something great. Often he takes an ordinary life, given over with constancy, and turns it into a blessing for multitudes. What matters is not the size of the starting point, but the faithfulness with which we respond when God calls us.
m.c: May the Lord bless your morning and go with you at every step of the way. Go out with the certainty that you do not walk alone and that even the smallest thing you do with love has value to God. Trust him, and may his peace guard your heart.
m: The story of Billy Graham reminds us that God does not need to begin with something big. A farm boy, a young man who said yes to the call of Christ and a life given over with constancy. Jesus taught this same truth when he compared the kingdom of heaven to a mustard seed, the smallest of all seeds, which grows until it becomes a tree where the birds of the air come and make their nests.

Perhaps today you feel that what is yours is little: a simple job, a humble home, a voice almost no one listens to. But God does not measure the way we measure. The psalmist expressed it with gratitude: “O God, from my youth you have taught me, and until now I proclaim your wondrous deeds.” Every person who has been taught by God has something to tell about his wonders, and that testimony is a seed.

How can you apply it today? First, sow something small: write an encouraging message to someone, share a word of hope, help a person without expecting anything in return. Second, pray for someone around you who does not yet know the love of Jesus, and ask for an opportunity to speak with them respectfully and simply. Third, do not compare yourself to anyone; faithfully do what God has placed in your hands.

And remember that growth belongs to God. We sow, and he makes it grow. You can head into your day without the pressure of seeing immediate results. It is enough to be faithful, to be kind and to trust. A seed planted with love today can become, in time, a tree that gives shade to many.

o: Lord Jesus, at the end of this day, I come to thank You. Thank You for the air I breathed, for the food on my table, for the people who accompanied me and for every moment I felt Your hand upon me. Even in the hard hours, You were near, and tonight I acknowledge it with a grateful heart.

You know how many times today I let myself be carried away by fear and by worries, as if the wind were stronger than Your power. Forgive me for the times I turned my eyes away from You. I now give You the burdens I could not settle, the conversations that left me uneasy and the decisions still pending. Take them in Your hands, for I cannot carry them alone.

Stretch out Your hand, Lord, as You did with Peter, and lift me up every time I sink. Give me deep rest tonight, quiet sleep and a heart at peace. Protect my family and all those I love, and comfort those who wept today. Tomorrow I want to wake with my gaze fixed on You. I rest in Your love and faithfulness, assured that You keep watch while I sleep. In Jesus' name, amen.
h: After feeding a great crowd, Jesus ordered his disciples to get into the boat and go ahead of him to the other side of the Sea of Galilee. He went up on the mountain to pray by himself. Night came, and the boat, already far from land, was battered by the waves, for the wind was against them.

Toward morning, Jesus came to them, walking on the sea. The disciples, seeing him, were troubled and cried out in fear, thinking it was a ghost. But immediately Jesus spoke to them: “Take heart; it is I. Do not be afraid.” Then Peter answered: “Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you on the water.” And Jesus said to him: “Come.”

Peter got down out of the boat and walked on the water to go to Jesus. But, seeing that the wind was strong, he was afraid, and, beginning to sink, he cried out: “Lord, save me!” Immediately Jesus stretched out his hand, took hold of him and said to him: “O you of little faith, why did you doubt?” When they got into the boat, the wind ceased.

Notice a beautiful detail: Peter did not sink when he took the step of faith, but when he changed the direction of his gaze. As long as his eyes were on Jesus, he walked; when he fixed them on the wind, he began to sink. And yet his prayer was short and sincere, and Jesus answered at once, without lengthy reproaches.
Those in the boat ended up worshiping him, saying: “Truly you are the Son of God.” That stormy night taught them that Jesus is not far from our waves, but comes to meet us in the midst of them.
t.c: End this day with a heart grateful for all you have received. What remains unfinished, leave in the hands of God, who does not sleep and does not grow weary. Rest in his peace, for he cares for you tonight, and tomorrow you will wake renewed.
m: Tonight, as you go over your day, perhaps you will notice there were moments when fear spoke louder than faith. Do not condemn yourself for it. Peter, who had seen Jesus work miracles, also sank when he looked at the wind. What matters is what he did next: he cried out, and Jesus' hand was there that instant.

The psalmist prayed in a very similar way: “From the end of the earth I call to you when my heart is faint. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I.” When the waves of life are higher than we are, the answer is not to struggle with our own strength, but to turn to the solid rock that is God himself, a refuge and a strong tower against the enemy.

Before sleeping, do three simple things. First, name in a low voice the worries you carried today and give them over one by one, saying: “Lord, this is yours.” Then, give thanks for three concrete things you received, however small; gratitude calms the heart and brings the gaze back to Jesus. Finally, forgive the one who upset you, so as not to take resentment to the pillow.

Tomorrow there will be new winds, but you already know where to set your eyes. God does not ask you not to be afraid; he invites you to bring it to Jesus. So rest, without carrying what is not yours to carry. The one who sustains you does not grow weary, and his hand remains stretched out toward you.
